To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the global mass/age curve for Phanerozo sedimentary rocks is the product of the superposition of three separate curves, one each for volcanogenic, nonmarine and marine sedimentary rocks, that all three curves are the product of the interplay of three processes, erosion, sedimentation and diagenesis, and that the global sedimentary mass/age curve is a record of the global sedimentary cycle.
the global sediment flux is greatest during the Middle Paleozoicum, Late Mesozoicum, and Late Paleozoicum-Early Mesozicum.

(1) the global sediment mass/age distribution shows maxima in sediment flux in the Middle Paleozic, Late Paleozic, and Late Mesozoics, and (2) these three maxima correspond to times of maximum sedimentary flux on the earth's surface, maximum sea-floor spreading, and maximum orogenic activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the relationship between the global distribution of Phaner ozoic sedimentary mass and the distribution of mineral deposits, and between the global distribution in time and space of sedimentary mass and that of mineral deposits.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mass of sediments deposited on the earth's surface has been controlled by three main processes, namely the rate of sedimentation, the rate of erosion, and the rate of sediment transport, and that the rates of these processes have been controlled by tectonic and eustatic processes.
the global mass of sedimentary deposits is controlled by the tectonic setting of the continents, the rate and direction of sea-floor spreading, the rate of orogeny, and the rate of sediment flux.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the distribution of sedimentary mass with respect to age has a maximum in the middle Paleozoic, a minimum in the late Paleozoic, and a maximum in the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous.
we have shown that the global distribution of Phanerozoic sedimentary rocks is a function of plate tectonic processes.

we have been trying to understand the processes that control the distribution and abundance of ore deposits in space and time, and we have been trying in this way to understand the processes of ore genesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the global distribution of Phanerozoic sediments is not uniform with respect to age.
the global distribution of Phaner ozoic sedimentary rocks is a complex function of the tectonic and paleogeographic evolution of the earth.
the distribution of mineral deposits in the geologic record is not random.
